reconcile.note: Gill reads John's 'eat the passover' as the later Chagigah feast, not the paschal meal the Synoptics say Jesus already shared with the Twelve the night before.

discrepancy.note: Strauss reads John 18:28 as placing the paschal meal still in prospect the morning after the Synoptics' Last Supper.

quotes.text: Again, it is said, xviii. 28, that on the following morning, the Jews would not enter the Gentile prætorium, lest they should be defiled; but that they might eat the passover…whence it would seem that the paschal meal was yet in prospect.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §121, on Mark 14:12 and John 18:28.

sides.snippet: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, \"Where do you want us to go and make ready that you may eat the Passover?\"
sides.verseText: On the first day of unleavened bread, when they sacrificed the Passover, his disciples asked him, \"Where do you want us to go and make ready that you may eat the Passover?\"

sides.snippet: They led Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and they themselves didn't enter into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
sides.verseText: They led Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and they themselves didn't enter into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
